title: Automated Nightly Payment Gateway Reconciliation & Variance Ledger
businessContext: A subscription SaaS processes $500,000 daily across Stripe and PayPal. Month-end accounting closes revealed a $42,000 discrepancy between the internal database and the bank settlement payout due to silent chargeback fees, unrecorded currency conversions, and dropped webhook events.
problemStatement: Design an automated payment reconciliation engine. The worker fetches the daily settlement balance transaction CSV/API feed from Stripe, parses all events (charges, refunds, dispute fees, transfer payout fees), compares against internal database order records, and outputs a three-way reconciliation report classifying matches, internal omissions, gateway omissions, and fee variances.
constraints: Detect 4 variance classes: Matched, MissingInternal, MissingGateway, AmountMismatch.
Calculate net fees and variance totals with penny precision.
Generate audit ledger entries for automated accountant review.
candidateTasks: Build hash map lookup indexes on both datasets by `orderId` in O(N) time.
Identify charges present in Gateway but missing in internal database (e.g. dropped webhooks).
Identify charges recorded in internal DB but not settled in Gateway (e.g. failed authorizations).
Verify net settlement math: `gross - fee === net`.
hints: Index gateway records by `metadataOrderId` into a Map.
Check both directions: iterate internal to find gateway matches/mismatches, then check gateway records to find orphaned external charges.

testCases.name: Detects variances and balances settlement ledger
testCases.explanation: Accurately reconciles financial records and isolates discrepancies.

alternativeApproaches: Using double-entry bookkeeping ledgers with explicit debit/credit journals (e.g. Ledger / Formance).
commonMistakes: Only iterating through internal orders: you completely miss charges made in Stripe that never reached your database.
Comparing floating dollar amounts instead of integer cents, resulting in false-positive penny variance warnings.
